text: stepped in cautiously, eyes scanning the room. Bookshelves lined the walls, packed tight with dusty hardcovers and rows of glass containers he didn’t dare inspect too closely. The desk in the middle of the tight space was heavy wood — lacquered and carved, unlike the folding metal garbage in the rest of the facility. It was the only room in the building that felt like someone claimed it. He flipped through a few loose papers on the desk — scrawled notes in a sharp, arrogant script. Diagrams of neurological pain centers. Shock vectors. Stress patterns. Jake snorted. “Of course you keep a journal.” He rifled through the rest of the notes quickly — nothing useful — then moved to the drawers. The top one held broken fountain pens and a torn patient file. The second, an unused set of syringes in pristine packaging. Next drawer — a pristine pair of metal restraints, polished to a fine gleam, resting on a folded cloth like a trophy. Jake grimaced and slammed it shut. “What the fuck is wrong with this guy...” He exhaled sharply, shaking off the chill crawling up his spine. He reached for the final drawer, fingers slipping off the smooth lacquered handle. Frowning, he adjusted his grip and tugged harder. No movement. Jake tried again. Still nothing. Locked solid. “One locked drawer in a building full of garbage...” He muttered, already pulling back. “Yeah. If I were an egotistical freak with a god complex, this is exactly where I’d keep the fucking keys.” He reached automatically for his toolbelt, cursing to himself as his hands hit empty air where a screwdriver should have sat. His last one was still somewhere under a gurney in Leon’s room, long gone. All he had left was a blunt file, a wrench too big for the gap, and a mostly spent medkit. No leverage. No finesse tools. He raked a hand through his hair, scanning the room for anything else — a pry bar, a lamp base, a chunk of wall maybe — anything he could use to break in. The drawer was solid wood, sure, but maybe with the right angle— He stepped back, testing the floor space. Too tight. He wouldn’t get enough leverage to kick it clean. Not without bouncing off the desk or losing his balance. Maybe the handle then? If he could crack the handle off and pull the latch from the inside, that might work. The walls hummed. A static pulse rolled through the floor, deep enough to buzz behind his teeth — followed by a low ripple of laughter that was too distant to echo right. Jake’s expression darkened. He stepped into the hallway, one hand already tightening around the file at his hip. “Hang on, Leon,” he murmured. “I’m getting there.” And with one last glance at the locked drawer, Jake turned and sprinted for the hallway, leaving the pristine office behind, and the locked drawer waiting. Chapter 4: Current Surge Meg had found Claudette just outside the main wing, crouched low beside a collapsed supply chest, hand resting on the handle of her medkit like she was ready to spring into action. She looked up at the sound of footsteps, startled until she registered who it was. She clocked the tension in Meg — the way she shifted her gaze around like she would rather be anywhere else in the moment. “We gotta go. Leave the gens.” She kept her voice low; no doubt she had also heard the Doctor stomping around in the distance. “Why? I was halfway done one of them! I was just headed back to—” “Jake wants us clear of the area. Apparently, Leon is stuck in one of the rooms and is taking damage every time a chase passes by.” “He’s down here somewhere?” Claudette asked, glancing down the hall as she stood. “Why aren’t we helping him?” Meg shifted uncomfortably. “Jake said stay a full building away. Said he’s working on it. I didn’t get a lot of details, just that it’s... it’s not good.” Claudette rubbed her arm, unease setting in. “I... thought I heard someone yell earlier. But I couldn’t tell if it was one of ours or just... you know. Fog noise.” She’d been partway through one of the three gens clustered around the central hallway when the Doctor had shorted the entire section out earlier. The static had crawled up her spine like a living thing, slamming into the walls and rattling the equipment around her. Somewhere in the middle of it, she’d heard something — faint, but sharp. A voice. A yell. Distorted by the charge. She’d heard that kind of sound once before — from David, years back, when a trial had gone bad and his hip dislocated mid-sprint. That scream had branded itself into her memory, and now it came crawling back from wherever she'd buried it. It had to have been one of the boys, caught up in the same blast she barely managed to get outside of. And if it wasn’t Jake... Had Leon been in there this whole time? Claudette hesitated. Meg was already trying to nudge her away from the area, but just leaving felt wrong somehow. “If Leon is stuck... and no one else is around... shouldn’t we at least check?” Meg didn’t answer at first, seemingly just as reluctant as Claudette was to abandon a teammate. Leon wasn’t the type to suffer quietly. He yelled when things went bad. He barked for help. He cursed at the Entity. And yet... no one had heard a word from him except screams. And even those hadn’t sounded right. “...Let’s check the doors,” she said finally. “Just until we figure out which room he’s in.” Claudette nodded, already moving. She didn’t run. But her pace had a purpose now — something tight coiled between her shoulders. Meg hesitated a second before following, footsteps soft behind her. They didn’t speak again. The air felt heavier with each step. —--
